description: prConcurrentLimit: 2 — allows one automated PR and one unmerged major PR to coexist. A single slot would let a major PR waiting for manual merge block the entire automated queue. rebaseWhen: behind-base-branch on automated rules makes the automated slot effectively serial (each merge triggers a rebase + CI re-run on the next), so two slots do not cause package-lock.json race conditions.

schedule: before 5am on monday through friday — Renovate opens new PRs only during the midnight-to-5am window on weekdays (Europe/Zurich). platformAutomerge merges a PR the moment CI passes, so the last batch (Fri 00:00-05:00) runs CI during Friday and merges before the weekend. lockFileMaintenance keeps its own Monday schedule.

rebaseWhen: conflicted (global) — major PRs sit unmerged intentionally; rebasing them on every automated merge would waste CI runs on a PR nobody is about to merge. Automated rules override this with behind-base-branch to keep the automerge chain moving.

vulnerabilityAlerts disabled — Dependabot handles security advisories instead. Its native GitHub Security Advisory integration links CVEs to the Security tab with GHSA references and co-locates with secret scanning and code scanning, which Renovate cannot replicate. Tradeoff: Dependabot covers only direct dependencies and is slower than Renovate would be, but the GitHub-native security workflow outweighs that for this project.

lockFileMaintenance.postUpdateOptions: npmInstallTwice — lock file maintenance deletes package-lock.json and regenerates it from scratch, and npm 10 gets that single pass wrong for the @noble/hashes conflict: pkijs (via webpack-dev-server > selfsigned) pins 1.4.0 exactly while @exodus/bytes (via jsdom 28, arrived with Angular 21 / NX 23 in #3189) peer-requires ^1.8.0 || ^2.0.0. npm hoists 1.4.0 to the root and drops the nested copy, leaving the peer unsatisfied, so every npm ci in CI fails with EUSAGE. A second install pass converges to the correct tree (2.2.0 hoisted, 1.4.0 nested under pkijs). Not skipInstalls: false — a full install reproduces the same broken lock. npm 11 resolves it correctly in one pass, so this workaround can be dropped once devEngines.packageManager moves off ^10.9.0.

npm version: Renovate takes it from package.json devEngines.packageManager, which it reads before engines.npm. engines.npm is deliberately wide (^10.9.0 || ^11 || ^12) so developers on a newer npm can install under engine-strict; resolving that range gave Renovate npm 12, whose lock layout npm 10 in CI rejects (npm ci EUSAGE: Missing yaml@2.9.1, #3458, #3459). The lock layout only holds within one npm major, so devEngines names the major that writes the lock: CI installs the same range via .github/actions/setup-npm, and npm warns (onFail: warn) a developer on another npm. Moving to another npm major is a one-value change there plus a lock regeneration; no constraints entry here.

Angular and NX: manual upgrade only (ng update / nx migrate)
TypeScript: tightly coupled to Angular/NX version
ts-node: major updates disabled — each major drops older TypeScript versions; must align with frozen TypeScript

ESLint core + TypeScript ESLint: major updates disabled — eslint 10 / ts-eslint 9 are coupled to the manually-managed Angular, NX and TypeScript versions; minor and patch updates are managed by Renovate
ESLint plugins: major updates disabled — a plugin major dropping ESLint 9 support would break the lint pipeline; majors are adopted manually alongside an ESLint upgrade
ng-packagr: coupled to Angular version
@ngrx/*: all packages are Angular-version coupled — upgrade only after ng update
@types/node: must match Node.js version used in CI and local toolchain

jsdom: exact-pinned in devDependencies and managed manually. It is not imported by the app — it arrives only as a peer of jest-preset-angular (peer jsdom >=26.0.0), so while unpinned npm was free to pick the newest release on every full lock regeneration. Each jsdom major moves both its engines.node floor and its peerOptional canvas range: 28.x wants canvas ^3.0.0, 30.x wants ^3.2.3 and node ^22.22.2. Because .nvmrc (22.23.1) satisfies jsdom 30's engines, lock file maintenance regenerated a tree with jsdom 30 against the canvas@3.0.0 stub in mocks/canvas, which npm cannot resolve (ERESOLVE) — Renovate could then produce no lock at all and every lock refresh stayed red. Pinning also keeps the canvas peer range fixed, so the stub version stops drifting. Bump deliberately alongside ng update / nx migrate, and move mocks/canvas/package.json in lockstep if the canvas range changes. If a jest-preset-angular update fails on an unsatisfiable jsdom peer range, raise this pin to the lowest jsdom satisfying the new floor rather than unpinning it. Revisit 2027-01: check whether jest-preset-angular still needs jsdom as a peer and whether the mocks/canvas stub is still required — if either is gone, this pin can be dropped.

Node.js (package.json engines): all updates managed manually — minor/patch must stay in sync with MODULE.bazel's node.toolchain and the Nix shell's nodejs_24; @types/node is also frozen, so any Node.js bump is a coordinated toolchain decision; the ^ range means Renovate would only bump on version outside the current range anyway, so disabling prevents partial updates
npm major: managed manually — not Angular/NX coupled but major npm releases have behavioural changes worth evaluating before adopting

CKEditor: both packages frozen pending full architectural migration (DEV-6294). ckeditor5-custom-build has no newer tags so this freeze is a no-op for it. @ckeditor/ckeditor5-angular v6 is low-value, v7 would cause ckeditor-duplicated-modules, and v8+ requires replacing the custom build with the ckeditor5 npm package and rewriting the footnote plugin — tracked in DEV-6294.
zone.js: maintenance mode — allow patches only (disable minor and major)
@storybook/test-runner: fully disabled — each minor release tracks a Storybook major and requires a matching Jest major; both are frozen, so any update is a coordinated toolchain decision
NX-wrapped tools: major version ceiling is set by @nx/* peer deps — disable majors until nx migrate lifts the constraint

eslint-plugin-storybook: major updates disabled — its peer dependency pins storybook to the same major, and storybook's own major is ceiling-locked by @nx/storybook (peer storybook <11.0.0) and @storybook/angular (peer @angular <23.0.0). It is therefore bound by the same nx + Angular major coupling that freezes the storybook packages above, and is upgraded in lockstep during nx migrate / ng update

@jscutlery/swc-angular and @jscutlery/swc-angular-plugin: fully disabled, exact-pinned, and moved together with @swc/core. The plugin is a compiled WASM swc plugin, loaded via swcAngularJestTransformer in jest.preset.js on every unit-test run, and works only with the @swc/core minor it was built for. It is a peer of swc-angular, so it must stay a direct exact devDependency: as a bare peer, lock file maintenance resolved it to the newest release, 0.23.1 built for @swc/core 1.16, against @swc/core 1.15 and every jest suite failed with "Failed to deserialize program received from host" (#3591). Package is v0.x, so the major-disable rule is a no-op.

@swc/core: capped at the @swc/core peer range of the pinned @jscutlery/swc-angular (0.23.1: ~1.16.0, patches only). The range is the author's ABI contract for the companion WASM plugin, not conservatism: overriding the peer breaks the jest transform, and a minor bump makes npm lock regeneration fail with ERESOLVE, so Renovate produces no lock and every npm ci in CI fails with EUSAGE (#3346). Lift this cap only together with a swc-angular + plugin release that widens the range, and set allowedVersions to that new range verbatim. Only @swc/core needs the cap: @swc/helpers, @swc/jest and @swc-node/register are not peer-constrained by swc-angular, and the @swc/core-* platform binaries are lock-only.
Angular-coupled ecosystem: major version must align with Angular major — upgrade only after ng update

webpack ecosystem: fully disabled. These four packages are not dependencies, only overrides (one webpack instance, #3083), and each override is set to the exact version @angular-devkit/build-angular pins, because build-angular deep-imports webpack internals (webpack/lib/dependencies/...) that move between webpack minors. A ^5 override let lock file maintenance float webpack past build-angular's pin: 5.112 moved AMDDefineDependency and broke build-storybook (#3591). On every Angular update, copy build-angular's webpack, webpack-dev-middleware, webpack-dev-server and webpack-merge versions into the overrides.

playwright-core override for @pixeleye/cli-install: fully disabled, held at 1.59.0. cli-install imports playwright-core/lib/server, a subpath playwright-core stopped exporting in 1.60.0, so pixeleye:ci fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED on anything newer. Renovate grouped this override with the root playwright-core and bumped it to 1.64.x (#3508, #3539); the stale lock kept the nested 1.59.0 until a from-scratch regeneration applied the override (#3593). The root playwright-core devDependency is unaffected and keeps updating. Lift only when a @pixeleye/cli-install release drops the lib/server import.

Major updates: PRs open automatically but require manual merge. Timing matters — merging a major before a release or production deployment could introduce undetected breakage that poor test coverage would miss. Human decides when it is safe to merge.
SWC compiler suite — all packages must update together to avoid ABI mismatches between core, helpers, and jest transform
Grafana Faro observability SDK — packages are released together and must stay in sync
ngx-translate i18n — core and http-loader are always used together
ESLint plugins — group patch/minor together; major is disabled above
Jest test framework and utilities — jest-preset-angular bridges Jest and Angular so it must move with the Jest group
Prettier and ESLint-prettier bridge (prettier is not in the ESLint monorepo group)
PostCSS + autoprefixer (autoprefixer not in postcss monorepo preset)
UUID
Test coverage tooling
Third-party Angular-compatible packages (not strictly version-coupled to Angular)
Automerge all dev dependency updates (patch + minor) — 3-day age guard prevents adopting a broken release before it gets yanked; dev deps don't affect production.
Automerge production patch and minor updates — 3-day age guard prevents adopting broken releases

Automerge github-actions and docker patch/minor updates — 3-day age guard matches devDep policy and guards against supply chain attacks on newly-published action versions; matchDepTypes: devDependencies does not apply to these managers so they need an explicit rule
